newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to limit loans to property developers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to limit loans to property developers.

text.p: Indonesia will limit loans to property developers for land purchases under the latest economic deregulation package announced on Monday, Central Bank governor Suradjad Djiwandono told reporters.

Sudradjad said that under the new regulation, banks will not be allowed to give loans to property developers to purchase land. The banks are not allowed to purchase commercial papers from the property developers issued to raise funds for the purchase of land.
He said the move was sparked by concern over loan growth in the property sector.
Banking involvement in the property sector was one of the items of concern expressed by the World Bank in its annual report on Indonesia issued last month.
"The rapid growth of property loans could endanger the health of the banking sector and stability of the monetary system," Sudradjad said.
"Excessive loans to the property sector could result in a mismatch in financing and increase the number of doubtful loans," he added.
He said the average loan growth of local banks was currently about 23-24 percent a year, while loan growth for the property sector was around 34-35 percent.

"In May 1997, property loans comprised 19.7 percent of total bank loans, while four years ago it was about 13 percent," he added. The central bank said in a statement that the rules would be effective from July 14 and apply to new loans.
